narrative.summary: Infosys is a financially solid, cash-generative services company whose growth has flattened to about 4% a year while margins hold near 27%. Headcount grew 1.5% against that, so the offer sits in a business doing more with roughly the same number of people. Compensation cannot be answered from any free structured source for the Indian market, and this dossier does not guess: the number to compare against is your current package, not a market median someone invented. The company's own filing is unusually candid about attrition, cyclical pay increases and return-to-office friction, and those are the three things worth pressing on before accepting.

strengths.text: Cash of $2.86bn, ROE of 36.7% and a 27% operating margin: no funding risk here
Margins are being defended as growth slows, rather than earnings falling with revenue
A deep US sponsorship record (1,900 LCA filings in FY2025) if a transfer is ever on the table

concerns.text: Revenue growth has fallen to 3.9%, well below the six-year 8.6% CAGR
R&D is 0.8% of revenue and 95% of staff are in service delivery — this is a delivery career, not a product one
The company names delayed wage increases and hybrid-work friction as attrition drivers in its own 20-F
Compensation for the Indian market is a genuine data gap, and a management change was filed three days before this dossier

questions_to_ask: Which client account is this role attached to, and how long does that contract run?
What was voluntary attrition on that account over the last four quarters?
Is the compensation revision cycle on schedule this year, and when was the last one?
What are the return-to-office and client-hours expectations for this specific engagement?
How does someone in this role move from delivery into platform or product work here?
